_readme: The client's PRE-ENGAGEMENT baseline — how the business ran before yourco touched it. Consumed by runtime/counterfactual.py to maintain a shadow model of the business as it would be running without the OS. Captured at discovery and NEVER reconstructed afterwards: a baseline written after go-live is just today's numbers with a story attached, and it would quietly manufacture whatever gap we wanted.
_theRule: A counterfactual is a MODEL, not a measurement — nobody observed the business that didn't happen. Every metric here states the assumption it will be projected under, and the module refuses to compare a metric that was measured today but never baselined (that would invent a gap out of an absence).
_capture: Ask two questions per metric at discovery: (1) what is it today, (2) which way was it moving and roughly how fast. Question 2 is the one people skip; without it the model holds the metric flat, which is itself an assumption and gets disclosed as one.
capturedBy: discovery call — client's own figures, not estimated by yourco

quotesPerWeek.label: Quotes written per week
quotesPerWeek.assumption: growing ~4%/month, the client's own read of their pipeline before engagement

quoteHoursPerWeek.label: Owner hours per week spent quoting
quoteHoursPerWeek.assumption: tracks quote volume — hand-written quotes take a fixed ~20 minutes each, so hours grow with volume

avgQuoteTurnaroundHours.label: Average quote turnaround (hours)
avgQuoteTurnaroundHours.assumption: no trend stated at capture — held flat

adminHoursPerWeek.label: Owner hours per week on admin
adminHoursPerWeek.assumption: creeping up ~2%/month as job volume grew
